note: Independently rejudged RFC 9687 Section 5: a NOTIFICATION is MAY, while closure after no sends within SendHoldTime is MUST. The decisive new TestRFC9687ValidSendHoldExpiresBehindBlockedKeepalive uses production-parsed HoldTime 90s and SendHoldTime 480s, establishes a live Peer, and holds its userspace write path so periodic outbound KEEPALIVEs cannot complete. Processed inbound KEEPALIVEs repeatedly renew receive hold, while the send deadline is unchanged. The same transport remains open and the session remains Established at 479s. At expiry the actual timer callback takes its bounded optional-notification path and closes the transport while the write path is still held; after releasing the holder, the peer observes EOF and the close cause is exactly ErrSendHoldTimerExpired, not ErrHoldTimerExpired. startSendHoldTimer/sendHoldTimerCheck drive sendHoldTimerExpired, and closeConnWithin reaches dropConn for the held path. The main-thread log job-rfc9687-completion-proofs-25e72061.log contains baseline PASS runs and a real mutant red: omitting closeConnQuietly(conn) in dropConn fails this unit's exact socket-open assertion at line 90 after its five-second observation bound. A write-deadline change or Run completion cannot satisfy that assertion. The old action-list writable-connection closure and pre-expiry live-session tests remain auxiliary observations; their shortened timer setup is not the valid-duration integration proof. The new valid 479s live-socket control supplies the conforming outside-condition case. This verifies the closure obligation for the exercised connection/write-path boundary, without treating optional NOTIFICATION delivery as mandatory or claiming an OS TCP zero-window experiment, whole-RFC release readiness, or fresh aggregate figures.
